openings.claim: A detachable wire tether bridle might retain the plate through tension while keeping it recoverable during inspection. This uses the second parent function alone; no guide, locating fence or contact stop is added.
openings.delta: Change the retention carrier from magnetic attraction to flexible wire connections between the plate body and bolts in the two existing carriage slots. Loop wire around unmarked plate regions and connect opposed tension paths only if available geometry supports them. Release one accessible connection for removal, leaving the plate tethered. Nearest ordinary rival: the supplied magnets retaining the plate.
openings.prediction: If opposed paths remain taut and their plate attachments resist sliding, tether retention should depend less on the spare plate's weaker magnetic hold. The magnetic rival may show greater spare-plate displacement or earlier pull release. Either configuration could fail; the supplied pull checks do not establish stroke performance.
openings.probe: First inspect routing and measure required wire length against 0.5 m. Proceed only if every wire segment, loop and anchor stays outside stroke clearance, leaves the marked edge exposed and permits edge-free gloved handling. Compare tether and magnetic configurations using at most three twenty-stroke runs and three timed removal/return checks each, with the spare plate in the final run and gloves during its removal. Mark initial position; measure translation and rotation-related corner displacement with the ruler. Require every observed displacement within 1 mm and removal/return within sixty seconds. Record pull release using the supplied 10 N scale where it can distinguish the rivals. Defeat the tether proposal if loops slide, slack permits excess movement, routing cannot supply opposed tension, handling exceeds sixty seconds or fabrication exceeds eighty minutes. Keep observation within twenty minutes; stop if informative measurements cannot fit.
assumptions: Slot positions and free routing allow opposed tension without forbidden intrusion; these dimensions are unspecified.
Available wire length, stiffness and reversible attachment capacity suffice; no such performance is supplied.
Bolts and loops can be manipulated with thick gloves without touching the working edge.

assessment: One uncertain tether opening warrants a feasibility check, then a bounded comparative probe. Recoverability alone does not establish positional retention; unsuccessful routing means no feasible test or deployment claim.
